q: Cathode rays are fast moving _____ emitted from the cathode of a discharge tube.
e: Cathode rays are fast electrons leaving the cathode. Cathode rays are fast moving electrons emitted from the cathode of a discharge tube. Do not trade electrons for protons or neutrons.

q: Cathode rays were discovered while studying the electric discharge through gases at _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Cathode rays were discovered while studying the electric discharge through gases at low pressure. High pressure or atmospheric pressure is not this quantity.

q: In a discharge tube, electric discharge first occurs at a pressure of about _____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. In a discharge tube, electric discharge first occurs at a pressure of about 20 mm Hg. Do not trade 20 mm Hg for 0.01 mm Hg or 760 mm Hg.

q: At very low pressure (~0.01 mm Hg), the glass behind the _____ is observed to glow.
e: The discharge that revealed cathode rays is a low-pressure gas discharge. At very low pressure (~0.01 mm Hg), the glass behind the positive electrode (anode) is observed to glow. Cathode or vacuum pump is not this quantity.

q: Cathode rays were first observed in 1869 by _____.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. Cathode rays were first observed in 1869 by Julius Plucker and Johann Hittorf. Eugen goldstein or j.j.

q: The term 'cathode rays' was named in 1876 by _____.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. The term 'cathode rays' was named in 1876 by Eugen Goldstein. Robert andrews millikan or wilhelm conrad roentgen is not this quantity.

q: In 1897, British physicist _____ showed that cathode rays are composed of a previously unknown negatively charged particle.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. In 1897, British physicist Joseph John Thomson showed that cathode rays are composed of a previously unknown negatively charged particle. Do not trade Joseph John Thomson for Niels Bohr or Edwin Hubble.

q: J.J. Thomson measured the charge to mass ratio ($e/m$) of the electron to be _____.
e: In 1897 J. J. Thomson showed the rays were a new negative particle, the electron. J.J. Thomson measured the charge to mass ratio (e/m) of the electron to be -1.759 × 10^11 C kg^-1. -1.602 × 10^-19 C or 9.107 × 10^-31 kg is a different relation from -1.759 × 10^11 C kg^-1.

q: The charge of the electron ($-1.602 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$) was measured by _____ in 1906.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The charge of the electron (-1.602 × 10^-19 C) was measured by Robert Andrews Millikan in 1906. Julius plucker or eugen goldstein is not this quantity.

q: The mass of the electron is approximately _____.
e: The mass of the electron is approximately 9.107 × 10^-31 kg. 1.602 × 10^-19 kg or 1.759 × 10^11 kg is a different relation from 9.107 × 10^-31 kg.

q: Which of the following is NOT a property of cathode rays?
a: They cannot be deflected by electric and magnetic fields
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. Which of the following is NOT a property of cathode rays? They travel in straight lines or they can ionize gases is not this quantity.

q: Cathode rays can _____ the gases through which they pass.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. Cathode rays can ionize the gases through which they pass. Do not trade ionize for neutralize or solidify.

q: The cathode ray tube (CRT) is a _____ tube that contains an electron gun, a deflection system, and a fluorescent screen.
e: A CRT is a vacuum tube with an electron gun, deflection plates, and a fluorescent screen. Gas-filled or water-cooled is not this quantity.

q: Before late 2000 AD, CRTs were widely used in cathode ray oscilloscopes (CROs), television sets, and _____.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. Before late 2000 AD, CRTs were widely used in cathode ray oscilloscopes (CROs), television sets, and computer monitors. Organic light-emitting diode displays or plasma displays is not this quantity.

q: CRTs have been largely superseded by newer flat-panel display technologies such as LCD, plasma display, and _____ displays.
e: CRTs have been largely superseded by newer flat-panel display technologies such as LCD, plasma display, and organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displays. Cathode ray or fluorescent is not this quantity.

q: Cathode rays are _____.
e: Cathode rays are invisible electrons. You see them only when they make glass or a screen fluoresce. Cathode rays are invisible. Do not trade invisible for visible or luminescent on their own.

q: When cathode rays strike the glass wall of a tube or a fluorescent screen, they can cause a glow called _____.
e: A CRT is a vacuum tube with an electron gun, deflection plates, and a fluorescent screen. When cathode rays strike the glass wall of a tube or a fluorescent screen, they can cause a glow called fluorescence. Do not trade fluorescence for incandescence or phosphorescence.

q: In a CRT, the electron beam is accelerated and focused onto the fluorescent screen to create _____.
e: In a CRT, the electron beam is accelerated and focused onto the fluorescent screen to create images. Sound waves or magnetic fields is not this quantity.

q: According to electromagnetic theory, a drawback of Rutherford's atomic model is that orbiting electrons will emit radiation and finally _____.
e: Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium. According to electromagnetic theory, a drawback of Rutherford's atomic model is that orbiting electrons will emit radiation and finally collapse into the nucleus. Do not trade collapse into the nucleus for escape the atom or form a new element.

q: Bohr's Postulate I states that an electron can move only in allowed _____ orbits.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. Bohr's Postulate I states that an electron can move only in allowed circular orbits. Elliptical or spiral is not this quantity.

q: According to Bohr's Postulate II, an electron revolves around the nucleus with angular momentum $L$ which is an integral multiple of _____.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. According to Bohr's Postulate II, an electron revolves around the nucleus with angular momentum L which is an integral multiple of h/2π. hπ or 2hπ is a different relation from h/2π.

q: Bohr's Postulate II is the concept of _____.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. Bohr's Postulate II is the concept of angular momentum quantization. Do not trade angular momentum quantization for energy quantization or charge quantization.

q: According to Bohr's Postulate III, an electron can undergo transition from an orbit to another by absorbing or emitting energy equal to the _____ between the two states.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. According to Bohr's Postulate III, an electron can undergo transition from an orbit to another by absorbing or emitting energy equal to the energy difference between the two states. Sum of energies or product of energies is not this quantity.

q: In a hydrogen atom, the centripetal force is balanced by the attractive _____ force between the electron and proton.
e: Centripetal acceleration is v²/r toward the centre. It changes the direction of velocity, not the speed, when speed is constant. In a hydrogen atom, the centripetal force is balanced by the attractive Coulomb force between the electron and proton. Do not trade Coulomb for gravitational or magnetic.

q: All the energy values of the hydrogen atom are negative, which means the electron is _____ to the nucleus.
e: All the energy values of the hydrogen atom are negative, which means the electron is bound to the nucleus. Do not trade bound for repelled or neutral.

q: The fine structure constant $\alpha$ is a dimensionless constant with a value of approximately _____.
e: The fine structure constant α is a dimensionless constant with a value of approximately 1/137. 1/273 or 1/300 is a different relation from 1/137.

q: The energy of a hydrogen atom in the $n$th state is given by the formula $E_n = $ _____.
e: The energy of a hydrogen atom in the nth state is given by the formula E_n = -(13.6)/(n²) eV. (13.6)/(n²) eV or -(13.6)/(n) eV is a different relation from -(13.6)/(n²) eV.

q: The radius of a hydrogen atom in the $n$th state is given by $r_n = $ _____.
e: The radius of a hydrogen atom in the nth state is given by r_n = 0.52896 n² AA. 0.52896 n AA or 0.52896 / n² AA is a different relation from 0.52896 n² AA.

q: For $n=1$, the radius of the hydrogen atom is called _____.
e: For n=1, the radius of the hydrogen atom is called Bohr's radius. Rutherford's radius or planck's radius is not this quantity.

q: The value of Bohr's radius ($r_B$) is _____.
e: Bohr put electrons in allowed orbits with quantized angular momentum. The value of Bohr's radius (r_B) is 0.52896 AA. Do not trade 0.52896 AA for 1.05792 AA or 0.26448 AA.

q: In a hydrogen discharge tube, if a high voltage is applied, the tube lights up with a bright _____ glow.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. In a hydrogen discharge tube, if a high voltage is applied, the tube lights up with a bright pink glow. Blue or green is not this quantity.

q: The ground state of a hydrogen atom corresponds to the principal quantum number $n = $ _____.
e: The ground state of a hydrogen atom corresponds to the principal quantum number n = 1. 2 or 0 is not this quantity.

q: The first excited state of a hydrogen atom corresponds to the principal quantum number $n = $ _____.
e: The first excited state of a hydrogen atom corresponds to the principal quantum number n = 2. Do not trade 2 for 1 or 3.

q: When an electron returns from a higher energy state to a lower energy state, it releases energy in the form of _____.
e: When an electron returns from a higher energy state to a lower energy state, it releases energy in the form of electromagnetic radiation. Do not trade electromagnetic radiation for kinetic energy or potential energy.

q: The radiated energy during an electron transition is given by $\Delta E = $ _____.
e: The radiated energy during an electron transition is given by ΔE = Eni - Enf. Enf - eni or eni + enf is not this quantity.

q: In the emission of X-rays, the energy emitted due to electron transition from $n=2$ energy state to $n=1$ energy state is called _____ characteristic X-rays.
e: In the emission of X-rays, the energy emitted due to electron transition from n=2 energy state to n=1 energy state is called K_α characteristic X-rays. K_β or l_α is not this quantity.

q: In the emission of X-rays, a transition from $n=3$ energy state to $n=1$ energy state is called _____ characteristic X-rays.
e: In the emission of X-rays, a transition from n=3 energy state to n=1 energy state is called K_β characteristic X-rays. Do not trade K_β for K_α or L_β.

q: When electromagnetic radiation of sufficient energy is incident on a metal surface, electrons are ejected. This phenomenon is known as the _____.
e: Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium. When electromagnetic radiation of sufficient energy is incident on a metal surface, electrons are ejected. This phenomenon is known as the photoelectric effect. Do not trade photoelectric effect for Compton effect or Doppler effect.

q: The electrons ejected from a metal surface during the photoelectric effect are called _____.
e: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency hits it. The electrons ejected from a metal surface during the photoelectric effect are called photoelectrons. Thermions or cathode rays is not this quantity.

q: There are no electrons emitted below a certain frequency of incident light, which is called the _____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. There are no electrons emitted below a certain frequency of incident light, which is called the threshold frequency. Do not trade threshold frequency for critical frequency or resonant frequency.

q: The threshold frequency is _____ for different metals.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The threshold frequency is different for different metals. The same or zero is not this quantity.

q: The photoelectric current is directly proportional to the _____ of the incident light.
e: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency hits it. The photoelectric current is directly proportional to the intensity of the incident light. Frequency or wavelength is not this quantity.

q: The kinetic energy of photoelectrons is directly proportional to the _____ of the incident light.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The kinetic energy of photoelectrons is directly proportional to the frequency of the incident light. Intensity or speed is not this quantity.

q: The photoelectric effect can be explained by the _____ nature of light.
e: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency hits it. The photoelectric effect can be explained by the particle nature of light. Do not trade particle for wave or mechanical.

q: Particles of electromagnetic energy in the photon concept are called _____.
e: A photon is a quantum of light with energy hf. Particles of electromagnetic energy in the photon concept are called photons. Electrons or neutrons is not this quantity.

q: The energy of a photon is related to the frequency of light by Planck's equation: $E = $ _____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The energy of a photon is related to the frequency of light by Planck's equation: E = hnu. mv²/2 or hc/nu is a different relation from hnu.

q: The photoelectric effect leads to the concept of the _____ dual nature of light.
e: The photoelectric effect ejects electrons from a metal when light above a threshold frequency hits it. The photoelectric effect leads to the concept of the wave-particle dual nature of light. Do not trade wave-particle for mass-energy or electric-magnetic.

q: A photon has _____ electric charge.
e: A photon is a quantum of light with energy hf. A photon has no electric charge. Positive or negative is not this quantity.

q: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different _____.
e: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different masses. Atomic numbers or chemical properties is not this quantity.

q: Isotopes have the same number of _____ but a different number of _____.
e: Isotopes have the same number of protons, neutrons but a different number of _____. Do not trade protons, neutrons for neutrons, protons or electrons, protons.

q: Isotopes have the same _____ number but different _____ number.
e: Isotopes have the same atomic, mass number but different _____ number. Mass, atomic or neutron, proton is not this quantity.

q: Because isotopes have the same number of electrons, they have the same _____ properties.
e: Because isotopes have the same number of electrons, they have the same chemical properties. Physical or nuclear is not this quantity.

q: Isotopes have different _____ properties as they vary in their atomic mass.
e: Isotopes have different physical properties as they vary in their atomic mass. Chemical or electronic is not this quantity.

q: Stable isotopes do not decay, whereas unstable isotopes are _____ and decay into other elements.
e: Stable isotopes do not decay, whereas unstable isotopes are radioactive and decay into other elements. Inert or ionized is not this quantity.

q: Isotopes can be produced artificially using nuclear reactors and _____.
e: Isotopes can be produced artificially using nuclear reactors and particle accelerators. Chemical reactors or distillation columns is not this quantity.

q: The stable isotope $^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}$ has 29 protons, 29 electrons, and _____ neutrons.
e: The stable isotope ^6329Cu has 29 protons, 29 electrons, and 34 neutrons. 29 or 36 is not this quantity.

q: The natural abundance of $^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}$ is _____, while $^{65}_{29}\text{Cu}$ is 31%.
e: The natural abundance of ^6329Cu is 69%, while ^6529Cu is 31%. Do not trade 69% for 50% or 31%.

q: The three isotopes of hydrogen are hydrogen ($^1_1\text{H}$), deuterium ($^2_1\text{H}$), and _____.
e: The three isotopes of hydrogen are hydrogen (^1_1H), deuterium (²_1H), and tritium. Helium or lithium is not this quantity.

q: Among the hydrogen isotopes, _____ is radioactive and transforms into the helium isotope $^3_2\text{He}$.
e: Among the hydrogen isotopes, tritium (³_1H) is radioactive and transforms into the helium isotope ³_2He. hydrogen (^1_1H) or deuterium (²_1H) is a different relation from tritium (³_1H).

q: The most abundant isotope in the entire universe is the hydrogen isotope _____.
e: The most abundant isotope in the entire universe is the hydrogen isotope ^1_1H. ²_1H or ³_1H is a different relation from ^1_1H.

q: When a source of light waves is traveling away from the observer, the observed wavelength will be slightly _____ than the wavelength of the stationary source.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. When a source of light waves is traveling away from the observer, the observed wavelength will be slightly longer than the wavelength of the stationary source. Shorter or equal is not this quantity.

q: In astronomy, a shift toward longer wavelengths is referred to as a _____.
e: In astronomy, a shift toward longer wavelengths is referred to as a redshift. Blueshift or greenshift is not this quantity.

q: A shift toward shorter wavelengths, which occurs when the source is moving toward the observer, is called a _____.
e: A shift toward shorter wavelengths, which occurs when the source is moving toward the observer, is called a blueshift. Do not trade blueshift for redshift or Doppler shift.

q: The main reasons for redshift include the Doppler effect, strong gravitational force, and _____.
e: The main reasons for redshift include the Doppler effect, strong gravitational force, and cosmological redshift. Do not trade cosmological redshift for magnetic redshift or thermal redshift.

q: Cosmological redshift occurs such that light stretches (longer wavelength) as _____ expands.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Cosmological redshift occurs such that light stretches (longer wavelength) as space expands. Do not trade space for the star or the galaxy.

q: In 1929, Edwin Hubble noticed that the farther away a galaxy is, the _____ it moves.
e: In 1929, Edwin Hubble noticed that the farther away a galaxy is, the faster it moves. Slower or more erratically is not this quantity.

q: Hubble's law provided the first evidence that the Universe is _____.
e: Hubble's law provided the first evidence that the Universe is expanding. Do not trade expanding for static or contracting.

q: Hubble's law formula is given as $v = $ _____.
e: Hubble's law formula is given as v = H_0 d. d / H_0 or H_0 / d is a different relation from H_0 d.

q: In Hubble's law, $H_0$ represents the _____ constant.
e: In Hubble's law, H_0 represents the Hubble constant. Do not trade Hubble for Planck or Fine structure.

q: The unit of the Hubble constant is _____.
e: The unit of the Hubble constant is km s^-1 Mpc^-1. Do not trade km s^-1 Mpc^-1 for m s^-2 or km h^-1.

q: A limitation of Hubble's law is that the observed velocity gets influenced by the _____ motion of galaxies.
e: A limitation of Hubble's law is that the observed velocity gets influenced by the intrinsic motion of galaxies. Do not trade intrinsic for light-speed or rotational.

q: The measured value of the Hubble constant is approximately _____.
e: The measured value of the Hubble constant is approximately 72 km s^-1 Mpc^-1. 100 km s^-1 mpc^-1 or 50 km s^-1 mpc^-1 is not this quantity.

q: According to the redshift formula, the redshift $z$ is equal to the ratio of the recession velocity $v$ to the _____.
e: According to the redshift formula, the redshift z is equal to the ratio of the recession velocity v to the speed of light c. Do not trade speed of light c for wavelength λ or Hubble constant H_0.

q: In the redshift formula, $z$ represents the _____, $\Delta \lambda$ is the shift in wavelength, and $\lambda$ is the wavelength.
e: In the redshift formula, z represents the redshift, Δλ is the shift in wavelength, and λ is the wavelength. Blueshift or frequency is not this quantity.

q: The Hubble time or age of the universe is defined as the _____ of the Hubble constant.
e: The Hubble time or age of the universe is defined as the reciprocal of the Hubble constant. Square or product is not this quantity.

q: The Hubble time is given by the formula $t_H = $ _____.
e: The Hubble time is given by the formula t_H = (1)/(H_0). H_0 or c H_0 is a different relation from (1)/(H_0).

q: Using $H_0 = 72 \text{ km s}^{-1} \text{ Mpc}^{-1}$, the estimated Hubble time or age of the universe is approximately _____ billion years.
e: Using H_0 = 72 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, the estimated Hubble time or age of the universe is approximately 13.6 billion years. Do not trade 13.6 for 10.5 or 15.2.

q: The Hubble length is defined as the product of the speed of light and the _____.
e: In vacuum the speed of light is about 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. The Hubble length is defined as the product of the speed of light and the Hubble time. Hubble constant or redshift is not this quantity.

q: The Hubble length is also known as the _____.
e: The Hubble length is also known as the Hubble distance. Hubble volume or hubble radius is not this quantity.

q: The Hubble volume is defined as the volume of the _____ universe.
e: The Hubble volume is defined as the volume of the observable universe. Do not trade observable for entire or invisible.

q: The Hubble volume is defined as the volume of a sphere whose radius is _____.
e: The Hubble volume is defined as the volume of a sphere whose radius is c H_0^-1. H_0 or (1)/(H_0) is a different relation from c H_0^-1.
